entries.title: Draft linear Gaussian density comparison
entries.statement: DRAFT comparison model: Let X be a centered stationary real Gaussian field on R^2 with spectral density rho^2 |k|^(2-s)/(beta a) on 0<|k|<=Lambda and zero elsewhere, using d^2k/(2pi)^2. The additive linear density is rho+X. Its variance is rho^2 Lambda^(4-s)/(2pi beta a (4-s)). This definition does not identify a Riesz Gibbs point process.
assumptions: A stipulated Gaussian model, not a microscopic Gibbs construction; draft awaits independent review.

entries.title: Draft correlated Gaussian negative-exceedance argument
entries.statement: DRAFT, unreviewed: If a stationary centered real Gaussian sequence X_n has variance 0<sigma^2<infinity and Cov(X_1,X_(1+h)) tends to zero, then for any finite rho>0 the values rho+X_n are negative infinitely often almost surely. The one-point probability is Phi(-rho/sigma)>0. Bivariate Gaussian convergence gives covariance decay of threshold indicators; the variance of their average tends to zero. No joint independence of cells is assumed.
assumptions: Joint Gaussianity, stationarity, positive finite variance, and covariance decay.
Author derivation complete in review packet; independent mathematical review pending.

entries.title: Draft positivity obstruction to exact Gaussian particle density
entries.statement: DRAFT, unreviewed: The nondegenerate additive density rho+X in the cutoff Gaussian comparison has a positive negative tail and is negative infinitely often along an equally spaced ray. It cannot have the exact one-point law of a finite particle smoothing with a nonnegative kernel. This rejects an exact additive-density identification only. Approximate fluctuation limits, nonlinear positive observables, and the existence of a hexatic Riesz Gibbs phase remain possible and require separate proofs.
assumptions: The stated cutoff Gaussian comparison with rho,beta,a,Lambda>0 and 0<s<2.
A finite point-configuration smoothing with a nonnegative kernel.
Integrable frequency density implies covariance decay; the ray argument uses the correlated-Gaussian claim.
No microscopic transfer, phase interval, or independent mathematical acceptance is claimed.

relations.rationale: The obstruction concerns exactly the stipulated additive Gaussian density and its nonzero variance.
Integrability of the comparison spectrum gives covariance decay, allowing the ray exceedance argument.
P0321 requires actual positional and bond-orientational Gibbs correlations. The draft only excludes one exact Gaussian-density identification; it neither proves nor refutes the target.
